name: liver
sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.

attributes.attribute: a very dreaded food among the Highland folk
a beast that would not eat a liver

text: The liver held a dark and old meaning in the north. Scottish Highlanders long kept a strong dread of it. They saw the organ as a food that was fit for none. Even the wild Water Horses of lore would avoid it. A lost victim's body could be gone and leave no trace. Yet the liver might stay, a single proof of what had come.

okr.objective: Record the old dread of the liver as a symbolic food in the hills.
key_results: Scottish Highlanders would not treat a liver as food.
The beasts of the deep also refused the organ.
A whole liver could be the only trace a missing person left behind.
